**Recursion in four sentences:**

Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller piece of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a simpler version of the original task until it reaches a "base case"—a condition so simple it can be answered directly without further recursion. Once the base case returns a value, each previous call uses that result to build its own answer, unwinding the chain back to the original call. A classic example is calculating factorials: `factorial(n)` returns `n * factorial(n-1)`, stopping when `n` reaches 1.
